concepts.title: Walk-in pharmacy with prescription delivery
concepts.rationale: Only 1 pharmacy is mapped in the circle against about 11.8 expected at the benchmark rate for 57,597 residents, and 19 rated pharmacies within 2 km average just 3.4 stars, so residents are underserved and poorly rated. With 63% of households without a vehicle, a pharmacy that delivers prescriptions and fills them quickly serves this area directly.
concepts.risk: Chain pharmacies with insurance contracts and lower prices may draw the same customers away, and reimbursement margins are thin.

concepts.title: Neighborhood bank branch with evening and weekend hours
concepts.rationale: The circle has 1 bank against about 15.4 expected at the benchmark rate, and 18 rated banks within 2 km average 3.4 stars, leaving room for a better-run branch. With 79% of households renting and median household income near $85,416, demand for everyday banking and rent-payment services is strong.
concepts.risk: Banking is heavily regulated and branch economics are costly, so deposit volume may not cover the lease.

concepts.title: Strength and cardio studio with drop-in pricing
concepts.rationale: Only 1 gym or studio is mapped in the circle against about 14 expected at the benchmark rate, and 20 rated gyms within 2 km average 4.5 stars, showing residents will pay for quality. A median age of 34.4 and 23% of households with children support daytime classes and flexible drop-in memberships.
concepts.risk: Strong existing gyms rated 4.5 stars nearby may take members, and high rents could squeeze studio margins.

docs.title: Review of Saraghina Pizzeria
docs.text:
Google review of Saraghina Pizzeria (5 out of 5, by Eli Eli888, 5 months ago): Broadway Pizza delivers exactly what you expect from a classic New York spot—fresh, simple, and satisfying. The crust is nicely crisp on the outside while staying soft inside, and the toppings taste fresh without being overloaded. I tried a slice with sausage and basil, and the balance of flavors was spot on. The sauce has a slight tang that works really well with the melted cheese.

The atmosphere is casual and comfortable, perfect for a quick bite or a relaxed meal. Service is fast and efficient, even when it gets busy. Prices are fair for the quality and location. Overall, it’s a reliable place if you want good pizza without overthinking it.

docs.title: Review of Saraghina Pizzeria
docs.text: Google review of Saraghina Pizzeria (4 out of 5, by Guido Hellberg, 3 months ago): Cozy place to have drinks and delicious food. We really enjoyed the atmosphere and the fantastic food. Their Neapolitan pizza is excellent and highly recommended. We also tried the focaccia, burrata, and melanzane, along with a salsiccia Neapolitan pizza. The service was also very friendly.

docs.title: Review of Saraghina Pizzeria
docs.text: Google review of Saraghina Pizzeria (5 out of 5, by bigbellynelli, 7 months ago): Absolutely beautiful! The margarita pizza was brilliant! I flew in from Utah to Brooklyn and this was the pizza I was looking for. Professional, prompt, and friendly staff, low wait times, and the ambiance is chill yet lively. Highly recommend!

docs.title: Review of Saraghina Pizzeria
docs.text:
Google review of Saraghina Pizzeria (5 out of 5, by Cait Mills Boyce, 5 months ago): Managed to eat 11 pizzas in 10 days - this place is TO DIE!  I’m a chef by trade and will just say I’m pretty judgy about tiramisu.  Saraghina hit it out of the park!

Back to Brooklyn in 2 weeks and this will be my first stop!  Love you guys!

Google review of Saraghina Pizzeria (5 out of 5, by Mallory Herb, 9 months ago): We got the fried seafood appetizer, a pasta, and carbonara pizza. It was an incredible meal all around! I was intrigued about the pizza but also a little nervous - it turned out to be amazing. I can’t wait to go back.
The deduction is because there seemed to be only one server on staff that night.

docs.text: Google review of Peaches HotHouse (4 out of 5, by Karen Gilgeous, 4 months ago): Overall the food was good. The meal I ordered was very tasty on the other hand my son who suggested we go there for his birthday didn't enjoy his choice of a chicken sandwich, he stated the chicken was under cooked and he only ate half of it. docs.title: Review of Peaches HotHouse
docs.text:
Google review of Peaches HotHouse (5 out of 5, by James, 6 months ago): This places is known for their fried food - primarily the catfish and chicken. I went with the catfish.

This was some of the best fried fish I’ve had, if we’re talking about just the fish itself. The breading is solid - going with a hot level of spice meant there was a good amount of seasoning on top, but I wouldn’t classify it as spicy. It was crunchy at points, but missing the flakiness and true crunch I’d associated with top-tier fried fish.

However, where it makes up for this is how good the inside of the fish is. This was spectacular - crazy moist, super tender, and just tasted fantastic. The complete opposite of that rubbery texture you get when you overfry the fish. The sauce that came with the fish was a little bland, however

As for the sides, I thought the mac and cheese was really good - cheesy, slightly crispy on top, and cooked very well. I also liked the grits - though a bit buttery. The fries were a miss though.

For the price, I think around 25 for the meal and a side is a solid deal. The sides especially come with pretty large portion size that will leave you very full.

Overall, this is very good Southern food that I certainly enjoyed. 8.5/10

docs.title: Review of Peaches HotHouse
docs.text: Google review of Peaches HotHouse (5 out of 5, by Sharon Lam, 3 months ago): Best meal I’ve ever eaten in NY. Been staying in Brooklyn for a week now travelling all the boroughs. Wanted to support black owned business and it so happened to be Juneteenth when we came in. The signature chicken burger was AMAZING and I subbed to sweet potato fries which were so crispy and nice. Even the house lemonades and iced tea hit so hard. Finished with the double chocolate cake and literally ascended. I went home and took a 1 hour nap before hitting the clubs after.

docs.title: Review of Peaches HotHouse
docs.text: Google review of Peaches HotHouse (5 out of 5, by Maryse Crevecoeur, 6 months ago): As soon as my friend and I walked in, 2 people greeted us and made us feel so welcome. May,  though, went above and beyond! She checked in, she made sure we received everything we wanted. She is the absolute hostess! This is my first time at Peaches but definitely not my last! The food was scrumptious but this amazing hostess is expecting us back! Thank you May! Your attitude and kindness are very appreciated

docs.title: Review of Peaches HotHouse
docs.text: Google review of Peaches HotHouse (5 out of 5, by Derrick Koch, 7 months ago): Went with my sister and was exactly what I needed for a soul food fix. It does the job that it needs to do let me tell you. I got the mikes hot honey fried chicken sandwich the chicken was perfectly fried the bun was perfect the slaw on it was the right balance. We also ordered a side of greens, Mac and cheese, and grits. All side were exactly how they should be if you ask me, proper comfort in each bite

docs.title: Review of Brooklyn Beso
docs.text:
Google review of Brooklyn Beso (5 out of 5, by Zora Middleton, a month ago): The atmosphere is super cute. Love the outdoor patio decor and vibe. Great r&b music while you drink a delicious flight of margaritas. They also have great BOGO drink deals on Tuesday alongside the tapas menu
Everything $7! Get a taste of everything for a beautifully low prices. Best tapas: oxtail Mac n cheese, bbq wings, Hennessy ribs,  & Cajun shrimp. They have other great items to try as well on the regular or brunch menu. They also have a digital menu where you can add the things you want to a wishlist so it's easier to order. Service was on point and will be back!

docs.title: Bedford–Stuyvesant, Brooklyn
docs.text:
Bedford–Stuyvesant ( BED-fərd STY-və-sənt), colloquially known as Bed–Stuy, is a neighborhood in the northern section of the New York City borough of Brooklyn. It is bounded by Flushing Avenue to the north (bordering Williamsburg), Classon Avenue to the west (bordering Clinton Hill), Broadway to the east (bordering Bushwick and East New York), and Atlantic Avenue to the south (bordering Crown Heights and Brownsville). The main shopping street, Fulton Street, runs east–west the length of the neighborhood and intersects high-traffic north–south streets including Bedford Avenue, Nostrand Avenue, and Stuyvesant Avenue. Bedford–Stuyvesant contains four smaller neighborhoods: Bedford, Stuyvesant Heights, Ocean Hill, and Weeksville (also part of Crown Heights). Part of Clinton Hill was once considered part of Bedford–Stuyvesant.
Bedford–Stuyvesant has the largest collection of intact and largely untouched Victorian architecture in the United States, with roughly 8,800 buildings built before 1900. Its building stock includes many historic brownstones, developed for the expanding upper-middle class from the 1890s to the late 1910s. They contain highly ornamental detailing throughout their interiors and have classical architectural elements, such as brackets, quoins, fluting, finials, and elaborate frieze and cornice banding.
Since the late 1930s, the neighborhood has been a major cultural center for Brooklyn's African-American population. Following the construction of the Fulton… (71 m from the pin.)

docs.title: 13th Regiment Armory
docs.text:
The 13th Regiment Armory is a historic armory designed by architect Rudolph L. Daus and built in 1892–1894.  It is located at 357 Marcus Garvey Boulevard (also known as Sumner Avenue) between Putnam and Jefferson Avenues in the Bedford-Stuyvesant neighborhood of Brooklyn in New York City. 
The armory building is currently used as the Pamoja House (also known as Sumner House Shelter Care Center for Men), a homeless shelter for men managed by Black Veterans for Social Justice, Inc. and supervised by the New York City Department of Homeless Services. The Pamoja House is named for the Swahili word for "together".
The armory's design is expansive yet austere. According to Francis Morrone, "Something, perhaps the busy-ness or a greater stridency in the machicolations, makes this armory seem more forbidding than the 23rd Regiment's which is actually rather jolly." (437 m from the pin.)

docs.title: Herbert Von King Park
docs.text:
Herbert Von King Park is an urban park in the Bedford–Stuyvesant neighborhood of Brooklyn in New York City. It was one of the first parks established in Brooklyn, from land originally acquired in 1857. The park was originally named Tompkins Park, after former New York governor Daniel D. Tompkins, and was renamed in 1985 in honor of Herbert Von King, a longtime local community organizer who was nicknamed the "mayor of Bedford–Stuyvesant". The park is bounded on the north by Lafayette Avenue, to the east by Tompkins Avenue, to the south by Greene Avenue, and to the west by Marcy Avenue.
The park contains a ballfield, a playground, and the Herbert Von King Cultural Arts Center, the latter of which opened in 1973. The facility also has the Almira Kennedy Coursey Amphitheatre, named after a longtime advocate for the facility's construction. (460 m from the pin.)

docs.title: Bed-Stuy Aquarium
docs.text:
The Bed-Stuy Aquarium (also known as the Hancock Street Bed-Stuy Aquarium) was a makeshift goldfish pond located on a sidewalk in the Bedford-Stuyvesant, Brooklyn neighborhood of New York City. The pond, originally formed by a puddle from a leaky fire hydrant, garnered attention from locals and the press at the time of its creation in August 2024. Local residents populated the shallow water with goldfish and colorful trinkets, transforming it into an unexpected community attraction. The project has since become the subject of both praise and criticism, with debates about animal welfare, urban beautification, and gentrification surrounding the installation.
The New York City Department of Environmental Protection paved over the space around the hydrant in the morning on October 25, 2024. A new aquarium located next to the hydrant was built days later, but was closed in December because it could not function in winter conditions. In June 2025, a fish tank was placed on a tree pit nearby the initial location, serving as a replacement for the original aquarium. (473 m from the pin.)

docs.title: Magnolia grandiflora (Brooklyn)
docs.text:
The Magnolia grandiflora is a historic tree at 679 Lafayette Avenue in Bedford–Stuyvesant, Brooklyn, New York City. The specimen is a rare example of a flourishing laurel magnolia growing as far north as New York, having been brought as a seedling from North Carolina and planted around 1885 by William Lemken. It is one of two trees that were made New York City designated landmarks; the other was the now-felled Weeping Beech in Flushing, Queens.
Beginning in the 1970s, it was protected by Hattie Carthan, who enlisted neighborhood schoolchildren to help raise money to protect the tree, which was threatened by the construction of a parking lot. After the tree was made as a landmark, Carthan founded Magnolia Tree Earth Center, a nonprofit focused on urban beautification and environmental awareness. The center is housed in the brownstone adjacent to the tree. (553 m from the pin.)

docs.title: Macon Library
docs.text: Macon Library is a branch of the Brooklyn Public Library, located in the Bedford–Stuyvesant neighborhood of Brooklyn, New York City. The branch, opened in 1907, was the borough's eleventh Carnegie library. Richard A. Walker designed Macon in the  Classical Revival style and the library was built from red brick and limestone trim with a slate roof at a cost of $93,481 (equivalent to $2,300,000 in 2024). In the 1940s, 1970s, and 2000s, the library underwent major renovations and repairs. Despite the changes, design elements present at the library's opening remain, including some bookshelves, guardrails, and wood paneling. Macon Library houses the African American Heritage Center. (750 m from the pin.)

docs.title: Capitoline Grounds
docs.text:
The Capitoline Grounds, also known as Capitoline Skating Lake and Base Ball Ground, was a baseball park located in Brooklyn, New York, from 1864 to 1880. It was built to rival nearby Union Grounds, also in Brooklyn. The park hosted local amateur teams in its early history, but later hosted professional and semi-professional games. The park's only season as the home field for an all-professional team occurred in 1872 when the Brooklyn Atlantics joined the National Association of Professional Base Ball Players. The park was flooded during the winter and used as an ice skating park. The grounds were used by local high schools and colleges as well, to play American football games, and ice rink football matches.
Many of organized baseball's earliest historical events took place at the park throughout the 1860s and early 1870s. The most notable event came on June 14, 1870, when the Atlantics defeated the Cincinnati Red Stockings to end their historic 84-game winning streak. Fred Goldsmith successfully demonstrated his curve ball at the grounds in 1870, a pitch previously thought to have been only an optical illusion. In an 1865 game, Ned Cuthbert is credited with inventing the slide when he tried avoiding a tag when attempting to steal a base against the Athletic of Philadelphia. In addition to baseball, the grounds hosted various events and exhibitions; most notably in 1873, when Washington H. Donaldson and two reporters attempted to fly a gas balloon across the Atlantic Ocean.… (756 m from the pin.)

docs.title: Killing of Henryk Siwiak
docs.text:
Around 11:40 p.m. on September 11, 2001, Henryk Siwiak (1955–2001), a Polish immigrant to the United States, was fatally shot on a street in the Bedford–Stuyvesant neighborhood of Brooklyn, New York City, where he had mistakenly gone in order to start a new job. After being shot once in the lung, Siwiak was able to make it to the door of a nearby house before he collapsed. The homicide remains unsolved; Siwiak has been described as "the last person killed in New York on 9/11", although he was not a victim of the terror attacks earlier that day.
The initial investigation into the crime may have been hampered, police believe, by the diversion of law enforcement resources in the city in the wake of that day's terrorist attacks, which ultimately killed almost 3,000 people. Since Siwiak was not robbed, wore camouflage clothing and spoke poor English with a heavy accent, detectives have speculated that his killer may have thought he had something to do with the attacks. Siwiak's homicide is the only one recorded in New York City on September 11, 2001, since the city does not include the deaths from the attacks in its official crime statistics. (769 m from the pin.)

docs.title: Nostrand Avenue station (BMT Lexington Avenue Line)

It was located at the intersection of Lexington Avenue and Nostrand Avenue. It also had connections to the Nostrand Avenue Line and Lorimer Street Line streetcars. The station closed on October 13, 1950. The next southbound stop was Franklin Avenue. The next northbound stop was Tompkins Avenue. The current site of the station is mostly residential with the exception of storefronts along the first floors of brownstones on the southeast corner of the intersection. (781 m from the pin.)

docs.title: Brooklyn Avenue and Tompkins Avenue stations
docs.text: Brooklyn Avenue and Tompkins Avenue was a station pair on the demolished BMT Fulton Street Line. It was originally opened on May 30, 1888, and had 2 tracks and 2 side platforms. It was served by trains of the BMT Fulton Street Line. Eastbound trains stopped at Brooklyn Avenue, while westbound trains stopped at Tompkins Avenue. The station had connections to the Tompkins Avenue Line streetcars. The next stop to the east was Albany Avenue, which was replaced by Troy Avenue at some point.  The next stop to the west was Nostrand Avenue. In 1936, the Independent Subway System built an underground Fulton Street subway station at Kingston–Throop Avenues between here and the site of the former Albany–Sumner Avenues station. The elevated station became obsolete, and it closed on May 31, 1940. (809 m from the pin.)

docs.title: Cultural Museum of African Art
docs.text: The Cultural Museum of African Art, also known as CMAAEEC and the Museum of African Culture Art and History, is a museum dedicated to African art and cultural heritage located in the Bedford-Stuyvesant neighborhood of Brooklyn, New York City. The museum houses one of the largest private collections of African art in the United States, comprising over 3,000 artifacts representing all 54 African countries and spanning approximately 4,000 years of history. It is one of only three museums in the United States exclusively dedicated to African art, alongside the Smithsonian National Museum of African Art in Washington, D.C., and The Africa Center in Manhattan, New York. docs.title: Albany Avenue and Sumner Avenue stations
docs.text: Albany Avenue and Sumner Avenue was a station pair on the demolished BMT Fulton Street Line. It had 2 tracks and 2 side platforms. It was served by trains of the BMT Fulton Street Line. The station was opened on May 30, 1888, and had connections to the Sumner Avenue Line streetcars. Eastbound trains stopped at Albany Avenue, while westbound trains stopped at Sumner Avenue (now Marcus Garvey Boulevard). The next stop to the west was Tompkins Avenue. During 1912 and 1924, the Dual Contracts program installed a third track on the Fulton El between Nostrand Avenue and the new Hinsdale Street station. Albany–Sumner Avenues stations were closed during that time. The station was replaced by another station at Troy Avenue. In 1936 the Independent Subway System built an underground Fulton Street subway station at Kingston–Throop Avenues between here and the nearby Brooklyn–Tompkins Avenues Station. The el station became obsolete. (893 m from the pin.)

docs.title: Renaissance Apartments
docs.text:
Renaissance Apartments is a historic apartment building located at Hancock Street and Nostrand Avenue in Bedford-Stuyvesant, Brooklyn, New York City. It was built in 1892 and is a five-story masonry building in the French Renaissance style.  It features elaborately decorated principal facades and prominent circular corner towers with slate covered conical roofs.  It has steeply sloped slate mansard roofs with terra cotta ridge caps and gabled roof dormers.
It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1995. (904 m from the pin.)

docs.title: A&A Bake & Doubles Shop
docs.text:
A&A Bake & Doubles Shop is a Caribbean restaurant in Brooklyn, New York. Owned by Trinidadian immigrants Noel and Geeta Brown, it opened on Nostrand Avenue before moving around the corner to a bigger location on Fulton Street in Bedford-Stuyvesant.
The shop was reviewed by ex-Village Voice food critic Robert Sietsema in 2018. In 2019 it was one of the five winners of a James Beard Foundation's American Classics Award. (908 m from the pin.)

docs.title: Girls' High School (Brooklyn)
docs.text: Girls' High School was a public high school in Brooklyn, New York. It was in a historically and architecturally notable building at 475 Nostrand Avenue in the Bedford–Stuyvesant neighborhood. It was built in 1886. In 1975 it merged with Boys High School; the new school, the Boys and Girls High School, moved to Fulton Street and Utica Avenue. (913 m from the pin.)

docs.title: Shaari Zedek Synagogue
docs.text: St. Leonard's Anglican Church, previously known as Shaari Zedek Synagogue and Congregation Achavat Achim, is a historic synagogue and church building in the Bedford–Stuyvesant neighborhood of Brooklyn, New York.  Built in 1909–1910, the building served as a synagogue until 1944, when it was bought by an Afro-Caribbean church in the Anglican tradition. The building has been listed on the National Register of Historic Places since 2009. (923 m from the pin.)

docs.title: Alhambra Apartments
docs.text:
The Alhambra Apartments is an apartment building at 500–518 Nostrand Avenue in the Bedford–Stuyvesant neighborhood of Brooklyn, New York.
The building was designed by Montrose Morris and built by developer Louis F. Seitz in 1889–90.   It is an early example in the United States of a multiple-family building designed with large apartments for affluent tenants.  The building, which features six towers and loggias, gables, arcades and elaborate terracotta decorations is across Nostrand Avenue from the architecturally notable Girls High School.
The New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission designated the Alhambra as a landmark in 1986. (946 m from the pin.)

docs.title: Nostrand Avenue station (IND Fulton Street Line)
docs.text:
The Nostrand Avenue station is a bi-level express station on the IND Fulton Street Line of the New York City Subway, located at the intersection of Nostrand Avenue and Fulton Street in Bedford–Stuyvesant, Brooklyn. It is served by the A train at all times and the C train at all times except late nights.
The station was planned as part of the construction of the Independent Subway System (IND)'s Fulton Street Line. Construction of the station began around 1929, and it was opened to service on April 9, 1936. Several of the station's entrances were closed in the late 20th century due to crime. In the 2010s and 2020s, the Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA) announced plans to make the station ADA-accessible and to reopen closed exits.
Nostrand Avenue has four tracks and four side platforms, with two platform levels. Express trains stop on the upper level while local trains stop on the lower level. This is because, in the original design for the station, the Nostrand Avenue station was slated to be a local station with only two platforms, and the current upper level was intended to be a mezzanine. The primary entrances to the local and express platforms in each direction are at Nostrand Avenue and Fulton Street. Another set of entrances from both sets of platforms leads to Bedford Avenue and Fulton Street. (996 m from the pin.)

docs.title: Nostrand Avenue station (BMT Fulton Street Line)
docs.text: Nostrand Avenue was a station on the demolished BMT Fulton Street Line. It was originally built on April 24, 1888, and had 2 tracks and 2 side platforms. It was served by trains of the BMT Fulton Street Line, and served as the eastern terminus of the line for a month and a week. Nostrand Avenue station had connections to at least four streetcar lines; The Nostrand Avenue Trolley, the Lorimer Street Line, the Marcy Avenue Line, and the Ocean Avenue Line trolleys. Under the Dual Contracts, the station was the west end of a project to expand the line from two to three tacks. On April 9, 1936, the Independent Subway System built the Nostrand Avenue Subway Station along the IND Fulton Street Line. The el station became obsolete, and it closed on May 31, 1940. (1001 m from the pin.)

docs.title: Reid Avenue station (BMT Lexington Avenue Line)
docs.text: The Reid Avenue station was a station on the demolished BMT Lexington Avenue Line in Brooklyn, New York City. It was opened on May 13, 1885, and had 2 tracks and 2 side platforms. It was located at the intersection of Lexington Avenue and Reid Avenue, and as such it had a connection to the Utica and Reid Avenues Line streetcars.  It closed on October 13, 1950. The next southbound stop was Sumner Avenue. The next northbound stop was Gates Avenue. (1007 m from the pin.)

docs.title: Tompkins Avenue station (BMT Myrtle Avenue Line)
docs.text: The Tompkins Avenue station was a station on the demolished section of the BMT Myrtle Avenue Line. The station was located at the intersection of Myrtle and Tompkins Avenues in Bedford–Stuyvesant, Brooklyn, one block east of the Myrtle–Willoughby Avenues station on the IND Crosstown Line, though there were no free transfers between the two stations. The station opened in 1889, and closed in 1969. (1022 m from the pin.)

docs.title: Sumner Avenue station (BMT Myrtle Avenue Line)
docs.text: The Sumner Avenue station was a station on the demolished section of the BMT Myrtle Avenue Line. The station was located at the intersection of Myrtle Avenue and Sumner Avenues (now Marcus Garvey Boulevard) in Bedford–Stuyvesant, Brooklyn. The station opened in 1889, and closed in 1969. (1024 m from the pin.)

docs.title: Troy Avenue station
docs.text:
The Troy Avenue station was a station on the demolished BMT Fulton Street Line in Brooklyn, New York City. It had 2 tracks and 2 side platforms. It served trains of the BMT Fulton Street Line. Sometime between 1912 and 1924, the nearby Albany–Sumner Avenues station was closed due to the Dual Contracts addition of a third track between Nostrand Avenue and Hinsdale Street. Commuters from that station were redirected here. It was served by BMT 13 trains throughout its existence.
The next stop to the west of Reid Avenue was originally Sumner Avenue. In 1936, the Independent Subway System built their own Fulton Street subway but did not install a subway station at Troy Avenue. The nearest subway stations to replace the elevated station were Utica Avenue to the east and Kingston and Throop Avenues to the west. The elevated station became obsolete, and it closed on May 31, 1940. (1025 m from the pin.)

Google review of Walgreens Pharmacy (1 out of 5, by Happy26!, 3 months ago): Held back for over five months before writing this review, but enough is enough.

This Walgreens is arguably the worst Walgreens in North America, and statistically it’s probably among the 10 to 15 worst Walgreens or CVS pharmacy locations in the entire US. That’s not just me saying that — plenty of other people clearly feel the same way. If you need even a basic prescription, I would strongly recommend going to literally any other pharmacy within a 50-mile radius, even if it means driving out of your way just to pick up something simple like Tylenol.

I get a couple medications filled here, and it is an absolute nightmare trying to get someone on the phone. You wait a minimum of around 20 minutes on average, and when someone finally answers, there is a very good chance they will immediately start being rude or shouting at you. Even when you speak calmly and respectfully, the attitude you get back is unbelievable. Simply asking when your prescription will be ready or why it has been delayed by two days is apparently enough for them to treat you like you did something wrong.

If you’re just stopping by to buy deodorant or basic store items, maybe this Walgreens isn’t that bad. But the actual pharmacy operation here is so dysfunctional that Walgreens corporate seriously needs to investigate this location and honestly consider shutting down the pharmacy section altogether.

The level of negligence here genuinely needs to be investigated. It is that bad. This is not me writing a review after one bad experience. I’ve been coming to this pharmacy for roughly 15 years, and over the last six months — honestly even the last two years — the service has become unbelievably bad. It honestly makes no difference whether there are five employees behind the pharmacy counter or nine. The experience is consistently terrible.

They do not treat the local community with respect. It does not matter how calm, patient, or polite you are when speaking to them — the attitude is consistently awful. If you need important medication, especially something that is considered a specialty medication, good luck.

I would absolutely not recommend using this pharmacy under any circumstances unless you are only coming in for something from the non-pharmacy section, like Gatorade or a bottle of water.

Google review of Amalgamated Bank (1 out of 5, by Katrina Hayes, 4 months ago): ⭐ 1 Star – Extremely Concerning Banking Practices

I experienced ongoing debit card and PIN issues with Amalgamated Bank for well over a year, and instead of resolving the problem, the bank chose to close my account after I repeatedly documented and reported the lack of integrity surrounding my card access.

My debit card repeatedly declined at Walmart, Food Lion, gas stations, and ATMs even when money was available in the account.

On many occasions I was forced to run my card 3–7 times before transactions would process. I was also unable to withdraw money from ATMs for months because the PINs being mailed to me did not work properly.

I requested different PIN numbers multiple times because the cards continued malfunctioning. Despite those requests, the bank mailed me the same PIN numbers repeatedly. Out of the last five PIN mailers, the same two PINs were repeatedly sent. I kept the physical mailers as proof.

Bank representatives on recorded calls insisted duplicate PINs were impossible because the process was “system generated,” yet it continued happening anyway.

After I escalated the issue through the Better Business Bureau and the New York State Department of Financial Services, Gillian McPherson Champion, Director of Branch Operations at Amalgamated Bank, responded to my complaints and acknowledged that representatives had provided incorrect information regarding the PIN process.

The bank also confirmed multiple “invalid PIN” and “exceeded PIN attempts” locks on my account while I was actively trying to access my own money.

Instead of properly addressing why my debit card repeatedly failed, why duplicate PINs were being mailed, why working PIN instructions were never provided, and why I was locked out of my own funds, Gillian McPherson Champion informed me that Amalgamated Bank would close my account at the bank’s discretion.

This happened shortly after I publicly documented these issues and filed formal complaints.

The timing of the account closure after I exposed ongoing debit card problems and inconsistencies in the bank’s responses raises serious concerns about retaliation against customers who speak up about account access and banking integrity issues.

Customers deserve accountability, transparency, working access to their own money, and honest responses when serious banking problems occur. I did not receive that from Amalgamated Bank. Amalgamated Bank is a bank that has discriminatory practices.

Google review of Planet Fitness (2 out of 5, by Michelle B, 3 months ago): ​I am writing to you today as a loyal Planet Fitness customer and to bring an urgent matter regarding the environment and air quality at your Bedstuy location in Brooklyn.

I addressed this matter initially with the staff  , and two members informed me the ac was turned down. This is unacceptable for paying members.

During my recent visits as well as today, I have noticed a consistent and concerning issue with the air conditioning system. The climate control is frequently being turned down or kept at a level that does not provide appropriate airflow or ventilation for the building. Working out naturally causes people to perspire, but the current conditions at this location are causing members to sweat excessively and unnecessarily. Today, when the outside temperature reached 85 degrees, the air conditioning inside was set extremely low—meaning it was far too warm—and I left earlier than normal because this facility has no windows that can be opened,. A properly functioning, consistently maintained air conditioning system is not a luxury, it is a health necessity. Without appropriate airflow, the air becomes stagnant, which allows germs to fester and creates an unsafe environment, particularly for members with underlying health conditions like asthma.
​
The air conditioner should be maintained at a consistent, cool level throughout the summer months, regardless of the time of day, much like the climate control standards maintained in hospitals or other windowless public facilities. It defeats the purpose of having a commercial cooling..

What stood out to me most is the contrast when comparing this to other Planet Fitness facilities. I also recently visited the Park Slope location, and there was a total difference in the air quality there; the environment was cool and perfectly ventilated. High standards of air quality should not just be limited to one location where everything is done correctly. It should be exactly the same across the board, including at the Bedford-Stuyvesant location, where the air quality is properly maintained at an appropriate level.

I would like this matter to be addressed immediately. I strongly request that management instructs all employees and staff members to maintain the thermostat at a consistent, cool, and safe level, and to stop turning the air conditioning down.  Staff should be trained to professionally explain that because the building has no open windows, the system must remain at a specific level to ensure proper ventilation, health, and safety for everyone in the facility. Simply lowering the AC and allowing the gym to become overheated is not acceptable.

Google review of PureGym Broadway Stuyvesant (1 out of 5, by Kevin Pineda-Gould, 10 months ago): Welcome to PureDystopia!

I cancelled my membership not because Blink was ever perfect, but because whatever PureGym has turned it into no longer resembles a gym, or frankly, a place meant for humans.

Blink used to be mediocre but functional: you walked in, worked out, tolerated the crowd, and left feeling better for having moved your body. Since the takeover, it’s been transformed into a bizarre TSA-meets-tech-bro experiment. You now have to scan into and out of the building through automated pod doors that regularly malfunction. When they break (often), people get stuck inside.

The irony is impressive: prices go up, staff quietly disappear, machines fall into disrepair, and the solution is more surveillance. Compliance gates. Zero human assistance. It feels less like a gym and more like a beta test for how much inconvenience and monitoring people will tolerate in the name of “access.”

Maybe I’m wrong. Maybe this isn’t a soft experiment in normalization and surveillance. Maybe it’s just staggering incompetence paired with corporate cost-cutting. Either way, it’s not something I’m paying for anymore. This is not the future, this is hell.

The session was thoughtfully structured to be accessible for all skill levels, ensuring that everyone felt comfortable and engaged regardless of their starting point.

What truly set the experience apart was the amazing queer environment (Zebra pattern hand wraps? Yes, please). It was inclusive, empowering, and provided a wonderful space for our group to learn and connect. I can't recommend OutBox enough for anyone looking to host a class in a supportive and high-energy atmosphere!

docs.title: Review of OutBox Gym
docs.text:
Google review of OutBox Gym (5 out of 5, by Mitch Candreva, 6 months ago): I went here with colleagues for a corporate sponsored ERG event and would highly recommend it to others considering it.

We did a basics class which was accessible and enjoyable to everyone who attended.

While boxing gyms and gyms in general can usually feel very intimidating, OutBox felt welcoming and friendly. :)

docs.title: Review of OutBox Gym
docs.text: Google review of OutBox Gym (5 out of 5, by Jaye Balentine, 5 months ago): Literally the best gym in the city. Julie is an all time great coach and the owner Max has created such an amazing space and community resource!

docs.title: Review of OutBox Gym
docs.text: Google review of OutBox Gym (5 out of 5, by T Yoshi, 6 months ago): An incredibly welcoming space with clean equipment. Everyone treats everything and everyone with respect. The boxing is a good workout and legit. Love it!

docs.title: Review of OutBox Gym
docs.text: Google review of OutBox Gym (5 out of 5, by Ellee de Baun, 3 years ago): Of all the boxing gyms I’ve tried, Outbox is definitely my favorite. Unlike other classes I’ve tried which are geared more towards getting a workout than actually learning the sport, the instructors here actually really helped me develop my skills as a boxer. I feel like I improved so much with just one session with Max. If you’re actually trying to invest in the sport I highly recommend coming here. Aside from the technical expertise, Outbox is also such a supportive and friendly community to be a part of. When I first started I was a bit intimidated but everyone here made it fun and the environment is really open and non-judgmental. 10/10 you’ll see me here all summer!!!

docs.title: Review of The Fit In: Strong
docs.text:
Google review of The Fit In: Strong (5 out of 5, by Alyssa Moore, 3 years ago): I’m so grateful that I found The Fit In. All instructors are all so kind, fun, and supportive during workouts. I love that there are three different locations within 20 minutes of each other and that when I buy my monthly pass I have the option to take classes at all three. Prices are also very reasonable, a month pass (4 classes per week) averages at $15 a class. They also have Pilates in the park, health events, and community happy hour.

I just purchased my third monthly pass and I’ve seen such an improvement in my strength and lower back pain. I can’t wait to see where I’ll be at in a few months.

docs.title: Review of Green Fitness Studio NYC
docs.text: Google review of Green Fitness Studio NYC (4 out of 5, by Evan, 7 months ago): decent gym with old school equipment. Usually very peaceful cause not many members. Place caters to boxers so if you're there for bodybuilding, know it is a boxing gym not one with a ton of unusual equipment. place needs to do repairs more often and mix in some new equipment here or there but the biggest issue with this place are the awful hours of operation. theyre open for like 10 minutes on sundays and close relatively early every day of the week.

docs.title: Review of Green Fitness Studio NYC
docs.text:
Google review of Green Fitness Studio NYC (5 out of 5, by BackpackingAndy, 3 years ago): This gym is like the song “I’m blue” except, replace the blue with green. If you like the color green, you’ll love the gym! Literally everything is green.

Jokes aside - this is what a gym should be. It’s personable, has a wide range of equipment to choose from, appeals to all types of gym-goers, has a lot of free weights and is incredibly spacious.

The dumbbells go up to 120 - and they are actually organized!

There is an entire two areas for stretching and ab workouts. Also a boxing area and dancing room.

Cardio equipment is modern and well maintained.

And the protein shakes are quite good.

Price for 3 days is $25 - I’d 100% become a member if I lived around here.

The only improvement I’d recommend for the management is to get the sauna fixed up. That’d be icing on the cake.

docs.title: Review of Green Fitness Studio NYC
docs.text:
Google review of Green Fitness Studio NYC (5 out of 5, by Ultimate Fitness, 4 years ago): Took advantage of the 3 day trial for $25. It was an amazing 3 days. I went to the gym between 9am-12pm, Sunday-Tuesday and the gym was EMPTY!!! Front desk staff has good energy. GYM MUSIC WAS GOOD!!! (which we know doesn’t happens often).

One issue I had was in the women’s locker room. While it was very clean, the lockers had no option for you to put your own lock or the digital locks didn’t work.

Overall a great gym space. It gives that “Haven/ Sanctuary” feel. Like the bar on “Cheers” it felt like home.

docs.title: Review of Green Fitness Studio NYC
docs.text: Google review of Green Fitness Studio NYC (1 out of 5, by Gladys Craft, 11 months ago): This place needs to get it together. Nice gym, but their hours of operation do not accommodate clients. First off, they recently cut their closing time from 10pm to 9pm, which disregards an entire client base of late night gym goers. Their weekend hours AWFUL. Closing at 2pm on a Saturday? It’s very confusing. For the membership fee paid, I hate feeling like I don’t have a gym that respects the variety in schedules for their members. And now closing early on Halloween? That’s ridiculous. Hire more staff to accommodate your members or just close all together. I have a feeling that’s coming next.

docs.title: Review of SNS Strength Bushwick
docs.text:
Google review of SNS Strength Bushwick (5 out of 5, by Justin Truong, 9 months ago): Been going here for over a year. Love that I never have to wait for equipment, the owner continuously looks for new equipment to add or old stuff to repair/improve, and haven't met a single bad apple there.

Great place if you want to head to the gym & have your pick of equipment. Lots of deadlift platforms, benches, & machines.

docs.title: Review of SNS Strength Bushwick
docs.text: Google review of SNS Strength Bushwick (5 out of 5, by Melanie Morgan, a year ago): So far, so good! I have never been a gym girlie and was nervous to sign up. I had a few sessions with trainer, Alan, who was very professional, knowledgeable, and helpful in jump starting my gym experience. I have since been going on my own and feel able to navigate the space and confident in my workouts. Generally, the patrons are friendly to neutral and doing their own thing. It's not too crowded and nice to have 24hr access. Thanks SNS.

docs.title: Review of SNS Strength Bushwick
docs.text: Google review of SNS Strength Bushwick (5 out of 5, by Rocky Dale Davis, 8 months ago): This was the best gym I’ve ever been a member of. When I first moved to Brooklyn I went to a few gym that were slammed pack and the equipment was just crappy corporate junk. Then I found this place, this would be a tremendous gym anywhere, but having it in the heart of Brooklyn it’s truly a gem. I’m moving now and will no longer be attending and I’m truly sad because this place and the people that go there are just awesome.

docs.title: Review of SNS Strength Bushwick
docs.text: Google review of SNS Strength Bushwick (5 out of 5, by John Burrell, a year ago): This place is gym Shangrila!  I have been to several gyms throughout my lifting life.  Upon my initial visit I was able casually able to walk up to a squat rack.  They have what seems like an infinite amount.  They have so many that if you wanted to do arm curls in the squat rack you could without impacting the gym goers while there(please don’t ever do that)! I have yet to see the 3-7pm gym rush.  The place is quiet and clean with plenty of the necessary equipment for any type of gym goer.  Alan and Tommy have a great product.

docs.title: Review of SNS Strength Bushwick
docs.text:
Google review of SNS Strength Bushwick (5 out of 5, by Ed P, a year ago): If you’re serious about training, Squat and Science is hands down the best gym in Bushwick — maybe in all of NYC. The fact that it’s open 24/7 already makes it unbeatable, but what really sets it apart is the atmosphere. This isn’t your average commercial gym with broken machines and crowded treadmills — this place is built for people who love to train hard, smart, and consistently.

The equipment is top-notch, especially if you’re into strength training, powerlifting, or just want to get stronger in a supportive, no-nonsense environment. Squat racks, specialty bars, calibrated plates, platforms — you name it, they’ve got it. The space is clean, organized, and clearly cared for by people who actually lift.

docs.title: Review of Bedstuy Yoga
docs.text: Google review of Bedstuy Yoga (5 out of 5, by Rachael Guynn Wilson, a month ago): I love this studio. Unpretentious neighborhood space, super welcoming, with superb teachers. I appreciate the range of offerings and the 45-minute class options for people with busy schedules. It can get pretty hot in the summer, but it's worth it. Personally, I prefer that -- and the kind of make-do attitude here -- to a fancier and more expensive studio. Please keep the class pack specials coming! It would also be awesome to have a fuller schedule to pick & choose from, but it's still a newish space and growing.

docs.title: Review of Bedstuy Yoga
docs.text: Google review of Bedstuy Yoga (5 out of 5, by Kaitlyn Rhodes, 4 months ago): I love every class I’ve been to, the studio is so inviting and really makes you feel accepted as soon as you walk through the door. However you like to practice and whatever level you’re at, there is a class for you! Restorative on Sundays with Kaylin brings rest, recharge, and connection to another level. Julia’s vinyasa and yin classes are so grounding, the way she guides and explains through each motion on an anatomical level just connects and makes sense for me. Rachel’s classes are so fun and brighten up any week, even in the dead of winter, they are the reason I first started practicing here more regularly! Pilates with Lisa is the BEST, the combinations are so effective and give you the perfect workout and the energy she brings is contagious. I’m excited to keep trying new classes, my roommate said the ballet and flow is really fun too. There are also community classes almost every day that are $16!! If you want a studio to just pop into or a space to practice regularly, Bedstuy Yoga is hands down the best. I can’t recommend it enough!

docs.title: Review of Bedstuy Yoga
docs.text: Google review of Bedstuy Yoga (5 out of 5, by Thalia Charles, 3 months ago): really love this studio, especially their restorative  and sculpt classes with Kaylin and Austin! every instructor is easy to follow & accommodating! i truly feel like this place is a place to go if you want a more spiritual yoga practice. i always feel like the classes leave a lasting impact on me

docs.title: Review of Bedstuy Yoga
docs.text: Google review of Bedstuy Yoga (5 out of 5, by Emily Innes, 4 months ago): Was new to yoga when I started coming to the Bedstuy Yoga studio months ago and have started practicing regularly thanks to them! Such a welcoming and fun environment with the MOST wonderful instructors. Kaylin and Louis are part of my weekly routine and their classes bring me so much calmness and joy, but all the instructors there are a pleasure to work with.

docs.title: Review of Bedstuy Yoga
docs.text: Google review of Bedstuy Yoga (5 out of 5, by Natalie Kurpeski, 3 months ago): I love this studio, I’ve taken several classes here:  It’s welcoming and spotless, the instructors are friendly and supportive. I am still a beginner and always feel safe yet I leave feeling challenged and accomplished. Highly recommend, it’s my favorite neighborhood studio.

docs.title: Review of Dou Yoga
docs.text:
Google review of Dou Yoga (5 out of 5, by Shakira Choonara, a year ago): This is a perfect little Haven. I tried many studios and held a gym membership in the area as well, but nothing beats my experience at Duo Yoga. It's a wonderful community, a place to slow down, breathe, health and learn to live positively. Each instructor is amazing, skillful and really friendly, so are all the staff there. Part of a #TravelGuruLife Expedition of New York City

docs.title: Review of Dou Yoga
docs.text:
Google review of Dou Yoga (5 out of 5, by Laura Rubin, 5 years ago): Such a warm and inviting yoga studio , with a neighborhood vibe. Some yoga studios feel like there’s pressure to be really advance. They support all levels. It feel safe to take classes indoors with masks - they set it up well.
Support small biz!

docs.title: Review of Dou Yoga
docs.text: Google review of Dou Yoga (5 out of 5, by Titi, a year ago): The 7/8am rise and shine classes are the perfect way to start the day. Often a mix of meditation, breath work and deep yoga poses. The instructors are knowledgeable and give great clues. The studio has a very authentic feel that I definitely prefer over “corporate yoga studios” like core power

docs.title: Review of Dou Yoga
docs.text: Google review of Dou Yoga (5 out of 5, by Kathleen Nolan, a year ago): I thoroughly enjoyed this studio. Overall a  wonderful class. Very kind teacher(Shieri) and front desk. I took the Pilates /yoga class and enjoyed the emphasis on core strength to start. Shieri had clear cues, encouraged breath to movement, and created a perfect flow to the class. Loved the use of props and the encouragement to do what feels right in your body. It was a very restorative class which was perfect. Something else I appreciated was they allow you to borrow a mat at no extra cost which helped since I was visiting from out of town.

docs.title: Review of Dou Yoga
docs.text: Google review of Dou Yoga (5 out of 5, by Lucía Ferrarese, 3 years ago): I’ve been coming to this studio for over two years, and couldn’t be happier. It’s a neighborhood studio and you get that familiar vibe, with classes for all levels and people who care for each other. Every teacher has their own style and they are all very good instructors. I’ve had to pause my membership a few times and management was always easy to work with and supportive. Thank you Dou!

docs.title: Review of Dean Crossfit
docs.text:
Google review of Dean Crossfit (5 out of 5, by Stephen Woodall, 2 months ago): I’m new to Dean CrossFit but already it’s been such a great experience. Everyone is so supportive and kind, I was genuinely surprised.

The coaches are really helpful and correct you when needed — shout out Juan for always correcting my form, I appreciate you!

Bottom line — it’s a great gym and community. If you’re on the fence or need a push — go to Dean CrossFit.

docs.title: Review of Dean Crossfit
docs.text: Google review of Dean Crossfit (5 out of 5, by Marielle Schweickart, 3 months ago): I did a drop-in Spit-Ups and Sit-Ups class while I was in town visiting a friend. I'm new to CrossFit and Juan was a super welcoming coach! Great balance of challenging and realistic for new moms. Thanks for the great workout.

docs.title: Review of Dean Crossfit
docs.text: Google review of Dean Crossfit (5 out of 5, by Nathaniel Dreyfuss, 2 months ago): After a little more than six months at Dean Crossfit (and several years at other boxes), I have nothing but praise for the gym—the WODs are sophisticated and varied, while the instruction and culture is welcoming and helpful, focused on your personal improvement, form, and performance. It’s a great gym, filled with great people, led by great coaches.

docs.title: Review of Dean Crossfit
docs.text: Google review of Dean Crossfit (5 out of 5, by Marnie Brady, 2 months ago): Pinching myself that I found the right gym, looking forward to being back soon. Christopher is the definition of a mensch, deeply kind with honesty and integrity. All of the coaches have been patient, knowledgeable, fun. There's a collaborative and community ethos here and that's what makes it especially great.

docs.title: Review of Dean Crossfit
docs.text: Google review of Dean Crossfit (5 out of 5, by Adam Albert, 5 months ago): Dean Crossfit is more than just a gym, it’s a community where you feel apart of a team. Not only do they offer crossfit classes, but they also have powerlifting and personal training and nutritional seminars. Ive been a member for 8 years and has been exactly the style of workout I want.
